To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the magnetic and electronic properties of Sr2YRuCuxO6 single crystals are governed by the itinerant holes introduced by the Cu substitution and the resultant lattice distortion.
Cu doping in Sr2YRuO6 induces lattice distortion and it increases the itinerant hole concentration.
the Cu substitution in Sr2YRuO6 leads to a lattice distortion, itinerant holes, weak ferromagnetic state and spin-glass state in the presence of superconductivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of itinerancy in the magnetic properties of Sr2Y(Ru1-xCux)O6 solid solutions.
the study of the magnetic properties of Sr2YCu1-xRuxO6 (0\leq x\leq 0.05) single crystals.
the influence of Cu on the electronic properties of the single crystal Sr2YRuO6.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Cu doping in Sr2YRuO6 results in lattice distortion and it is responsible for the itinerant holes which in turn results in a superconducting state with weak ferromagnetic and spin glass characteristics.
the Ru5+ spins are not frozen and the Cu2+ spins are frozen at low temperatures and the system is in a spin-glass state.
Cu doping in the Sr2YRuO6 crystal results in a spin-glass state with weak superconductivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic behavior of the Sr2YRuO6 crystal changes from antiferromagnetic to superconducting in the presence of a very small amount of Cu and the magnetic behavior is dominated by the Ru5+ spins.

the itinerant holes and the Cu doping in the lattice result in the magnetic and superconducting behavior of the Sr2YRuO6 crystal and the itinerant Ru5+ spins are responsible for the magnetic behavior of the Cu doped crystals.
the magnetic properties are a direct result of the lattice distortion and the Cu induced itinerant holes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic behavior of these crystals depends on the itinerant holes and the lattice distortion.
Cu substitution in the RuO6 octahedra in Sr2YRuO6 leads to lattice distortions that are reflected in the magnetic properties of these compounds.
itinerancy in the Cu-doped Sr2YRuO6 crystals leads to the formation of spontaneous vortex states that can be used for spintronics applications.
